Shareholders approved reverse-split authorization, allowing the board to execute a 1-for-2 to 1-for-50 split at its discretion. The move is intended to help meet Nasdaq or NYSE minimum share-price requirements and support a potential up-listing.

Shareholders elected Sumit Kapur, William Klitgaard and Clark Golestani to the board, and approved executive compensation, the appointment of Weinberg & Company as auditor, and a three-year frequency for future say-on-pay votes.

CEO Sumit Kapur said a possible exchange listing is part of a broader growth strategy involving the Quantum Pilot platform, expanded commercial and scientific teams, intellectual-property development, and partnerships with NVIDIA, QuEra and IBM. No timing or reverse-split ratio was provided.

Zapata Quantum (OTCMKTS:ZPTA) shareholders approved a reverse stock split authorization, elected three directors and supported the company's executive-compensation proposals at its 2026 annual meeting.

The virtual-only meeting was led by Chief Executive Officer Sumit Kapur, who said the company had a quorum and that six proposals were before shareholders. The company said final voting results would be reported in a Form 8-K in the coming days.

Directors Elected

→ Morgan Stanley Is Bullish on Apple—But With a Catch

Shareholders elected Kapur, William Klitgaard and Clark Golestani as directors. The nominees will serve one-, two- or three-year terms consistent with their designated board classes, according to the meeting agenda.

Kapur received 137.95 million votes for election and 71,624 votes withheld.

Klitgaard received 137.94 million votes for election and 76,037 votes withheld.

Golestani received 137.87 million votes for election and 147,899 votes withheld.

Each nominee also had approximately 8.6 million broker non-votes. Beth W. VanDerbeck, the meeting's inspector of election, said the directors were elected subject to final confirmation.

Reverse Split Authorization Approved

→ The AI Boom's Next Big Winners May Wear Hard Hats

Shareholders also approved amendments to the company's certificate of incorporation that would allow the board to implement a reverse stock split at a ratio ranging from 1-for-2 to 1-for-50. The board will retain discretion over whether to proceed and the specific ratio selected.

The stated purpose of the authorization is to achieve the minimum per-share price required for listing on a national exchange operated by Nasdaq or the New York Stock Exchange. The proposal received approximately 142.82 million votes in favor, 3.03 million votes against and 767,420 abstentions. VanDerbeck said votes in favor represented approximately 60.98% of shares voted on the proposal.

title: How Much Growth Are You Paying For In Palantir Stock?

How Much Growth Are You Paying For In Palantir Stock?

Palantir (PLTR) stock has gained 57% in three months, outpacing the 2.8% return for the S&P 500. On October 8, 2026, Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to buy from neutral. Investors who already own the shares now face a choice between taking some profit and buying more after a big run. So how much growth are you paying for at today's price?

You Are Paying For A Much Bigger Palantir

Palantir stock trades at 158.1 times its earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 21.5 for the S&P 500. Because a price-to-earnings ratio measures the number of years of today's profit you pay for each share, anyone buying at such a high ratio is counting on profit to grow.

How much would it have to grow? If the share price stayed where it is, Palantir's profit would need to be about seven times larger before the stock was priced in line with the index. That is the size of company today's buyers are counting on.

Palantir's Sales Almost Doubled In A Year

Revenue grew 93% in the second quarter of 2026. Management called this the highest growth rate the company has reported. Over the past three years, Palantir's revenue grew 46.3% a year on average, easily beating the 5.8% mark for the S&P 500. This means the business is growing faster now than it did when it was smaller.

Most of that growth came from the United States, a market that now brings in over 81% of revenue. U.S. commercial revenue, representing the sales Palantir makes to U.S. businesses rather than government agencies, grew 149% from a year earlier. That may be what buyers at today's price are betting on.

What Could Change The Price Of Palantir Stock?

A slowdown among U.S. customers would matter most, since most of Palantir's growth is there. On August 3, 2026, management said its goal is to grow the whole business as fast as its U.S. commercial sales, or faster, for 18 months. Management called that a very high goal. At the end of the second quarter, Palantir's remaining deal value stood at $13.1 billion, up 83% from a year earlier.

Abroad, the picture is weaker. Palantir's international commercial revenue grew 26% in the same quarter, and management noted in August that growth in Europe is poor.

The stock has also fallen hard when markets turned. During the 2022 inflation shock, Palantir stock fell 64% from peak to trough, compared with 24% for the S&P 500.

Palantir's report for the third quarter of 2026 is the next result to watch. Management guided revenue of $2.16 billion to $2.164 billion for that quarter, up from the $1.935 billion it reported for the second quarter. A result well above that range would show Palantir's sales growing faster than management forecast. Conversely, a result inside or below the range would show sales growing no faster than management forecast.

title: IBM Consulting Grew Profit 15% on Nearly Flat Sales. Can That Continue?
detail:
IBM Consulting Grew Profit 15% on Nearly Flat Sales. Can That Continue?
Habib Ur Rehman
Fri, October 9, 2026 at 12:05 PM EDT 3 min read
IBM
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM) produced a useful surprise inside its consulting business: second-quarter segment profit rose 15.1%, although revenue increased just 0.2%. Improving delivery economics can lift earnings, but repeated margin expansion becomes harder when sales barely move.

The July 22 results and quarterly filing showed $647 million of consulting segment profit on $5.327 billion of revenue. A year earlier, profit was $562 million. IBM attributed the improvement primarily to productivity actions, partly offset by investment in innovation.

IBM ranked ninth in our recent cybersecurity screen. See which security-focused alternatives ranked higher on analyst target upside than this diversified enterprise-technology company.

IBM Consulting Grew Profit 15% on Nearly Flat Sales. Can That Continue?

For illustration purposes only: work on a laptop.

Each margin point has a measurable payoff

At the reported revenue base, one percentage point of consulting margin represents $53.3 million of quarterly segment profit. A one-point retreat would absorb more than three-fifths of the quarter's $85 million year-over-year profit gain. This is a sensitivity calculation, not a forecast.

Consulting gross margin also improved, to 28.9% from 27.5%. That places part of the gain in the economics of delivering client work. Better utilization and more efficient delivery can preserve profit without requiring a surge in billings.

Our Amazon margin analysis puts a dollar value on similar segment-level efficiency gains and shows why the whole-company valuation still needs a separate test.

There is supporting demand evidence. Consulting signings increased 5% as reported, and the trailing book-to-bill ratio was 1.05. Those indicators could help sales resume growing. Their conversion depends on project timing and customer commitments; signings are management estimates rather than a standardized revenue measure.

A book-to-bill ratio just above one indicates that trailing signings modestly exceeded revenue, not that revenue is about to accelerate by the same percentage. Contract duration and the pace of work can separate bookings from sales for several quarters. Demand conversion matters because efficiency gains eventually become a tougher year-over-year comparison.

Better delivery economics need a durable customer base

A falling cost base can reward shareholders even before demand accelerates. The bear case is that further efficiency gains become harder to achieve, or customers retain some benefit through lower prices.

Repeating 15% profit growth with a flat margin would require roughly 15% revenue growth, far above this quarter's pace. With flat revenue, it would instead require the segment margin to rise from about 12.1% to 14.0%. These alternatives illustrate the burden of sustaining the profit growth rate; neither is management guidance.

A $250,000 dividend portfolio throwing off about $8,471 a year loses roughly $2,033 to the IRS annually if that income is taxed at the 24% ordinary rate. The full amount stays in the account within a Roth IRA.

Bigc Studio / Shutterstock.com
Qualified Versus Ordinary Dividends Set the Size of the Gap

For tax year 2026, the 24% bracket covers income over $105,700 ($211,400 for married couples filing jointly) for single filers. Ordinary dividends, including most BDC and REIT payouts, face that rate. Qualified dividends face a maximum rate of 0%, 15%, or 20%, but only if you held the shares more than 60 days during the 121-day period around the ex-dividend date. Neither schedule applies in a Roth, because qualified withdrawals come out untaxed.

All six stocks below are C-corporations whose dividends generally qualify, so a 24% filer meeting the holding period realistically pays 15%. The ordinary-rate column shows what the same income costs when the holding period is missed, or what a BDC or mortgage REIT of equal yield would cost.

International Business Machines Corporation IBM has launched IBM Ready for SAP SE SAP Solutions to help midsize and fast-growing businesses modernize their enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, improve productivity and support business growth.

Under the program, IBM will combine its industry expertise, fit-to-standard implementation approach and IBM Consulting Advantage, its artificial intelligence (AI)-powered consulting delivery platform, to accelerate the adoption of SAP Cloud ERP. The offering aims to simplify business processes, integrate enterprise data and help organizations manage their growing operations.

IBM helped Volumetric Building Companies reduce operational cycle times by 50% across purchasing, manufacturing and inventory processes after a three-month SAP Cloud ERP transformation. Meanwhile, the company also supported Second Nature Brands in integrating its acquired Voortman Bakery business into a common enterprise platform.

According to research from the IBM Institute for Business Value, 68% of enterprises consider accelerating ERP modernization important for improving operational efficiency and maintaining competitiveness. The findings highlight the growing importance of modern enterprise systems and reinforce the company's efforts to help businesses streamline operations, support growth and prepare for future AI applications.

How Are Competitors Advancing?

IBM faces competition from Microsoft Corporation MSFT and Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN. Microsoft is expanding its Dynamics 365 ERP software with AI tools to automate finance, supply chain and business operations. The company is developing AI agents that can analyze data and handle routine business tasks. Microsoft aims to help businesses automate workflows, track financial performance and manage supply chain activities through its connected ERP systems.

Amazon Web Services is helping businesses integrate AI tools with SAP ERP systems to automate business tasks. The company introduced tools helping AI agents securely access enterprise data and work across business applications. Amazon is expanding its cloud and AI services to help organizations modernize legacy systems, improve data management and streamline business operations.

title: IBM (IBM) Saw Mainframes Fall 42%. Is That Already Priced In at 18 Times Earnings?
detail:
IBM (IBM) Saw Mainframes Fall 42%. Is That Already Priced In at 18 Times Earnings?
Maham Fatima
Fri, October 9, 2026 at 9:29 AM EDT 4 min read
IBM
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Two halves of the same company just moved in opposite directions. International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) saw its IBM Z mainframe line fall 42% in fiscal Q2 2026, while distributed infrastructure, which covers Power and Storage, jumped 37%. Total revenue rose only 1% to $17.2 billion, and management updated its full-year outlook to 4% to 5% constant-currency growth.

IBM sells software (Red Hat, data tools, automation), consulting, and the infrastructure that runs big companies' systems. Software is its highest-margin segment, with a 32.2% segment profit margin. Whether the miss is a pothole or a warning depends less on the mainframe number than on what software does next, and on whether 18 times earnings already reflects it.

IBM (IBM) Saw Mainframes Fall 42%. Is That Already Priced In at 18 Times Earnings?
Margins Tell the Story

The moat shows up in the economics rather than the marketing. Software carried an 82.6% gross margin in the quarter, and its segment profit margin improved from 31.1% a year earlier. Red Hat, the open-source arm, grew 11%, and the data business grew 19%.

Even after the miss, the balance sheet showed $16,160 million of current deferred income (billed to clients, not yet counted as revenue), a sign the contract base hasn't evaporated. For investors looking past high-flying multiples, reviewing the best 52-week low technology stocks offers a look at beaten-down alternatives.

A Pause, Not a Collapse

Zoom out and the mainframe slump looks more like a pause than a collapse. Infrastructure revenue rose 1.9% across the first half even after falling 7% in the second quarter. Power and Storage ended the quarter with an order backlog (committed but undelivered orders) of nearly $500 million.

IBM has also kept spending on what comes next. Since the report, it unveiled a dual-architecture mainframe processor, designed to let companies run operating systems and applications on both IBM and Arm platforms. It also closed its purchase of HRL Laboratories, a research institution spanning quantum computing and advanced electronics, and plans to invest more than $10 billion in quantum over five years. None of that pays off soon, but it suggests the moat is holding rather than eroding.

Is Software the Real Problem?

The tougher question for bulls is software, the business that has to carry growth. It grew 5% in fiscal Q2, slower than the 7.9% pace across the first half, and Transaction Processing, one of its lines, shrank 8%. Consulting was flat at $5.3 billion. Free cash flow of $2.5 billion slipped $0.3 billion from a year earlier, and debt totals $62.0 billion after $10.5 billion of acquisitions this year.
